The given statements provide a series of direct ancestor/descendant relations. These can be modeled as a directed graph with an edge from each person to their direct descendants. Transitive paths in this graph then correspond to indirect ancestry.

Converting every statement into "X is an ancestor of Y" form produces the edges needed for chaining. Two disjoint paths both reach Jack:
- Ruth reaches Jack via the path Ruth \(\to\) Rebecca \(\to\) Noah \(\to\) Henry \(\to\) Diane \(\to\) Martha \(\to\) Amanda \(\to\) Kimberly \(\to\) Elizabeth \(\to\) Sandra \(\to\) Kenneth \(\to\) Joyce \(\to\) Marilyn \(\to\) Robert \(\to\) Jeremy \(\to\) Katherine \(\to\) Carl \(\to\) Kelly \(\to\) Joan \(\to\) Helen \(\to\) Adam \(\to\) Matthew \(\to\) Jack.
- Gerald reaches Jack via the path Gerald \(\to\) Gary \(\to\) Jonathan \(\to\) Carol \(\to\) Arthur \(\to\) Steven \(\to\) Grace \(\to\) Karen \(\to\) Andrew \(\to\) Bradley \(\to\) Ralph \(\to\) Joe \(\to\) Ann \(\to\) George \(\to\) Sara \(\to\) Mason \(\to\) Catherine \(\to\) Theresa \(\to\) Evelyn \(\to\) Debra \(\to\) Janet \(\to\) Julie \(\to\) Virginia \(\to\) Harold \(\to\) Samuel \(\to\) Frank \(\to\) Susan \(\to\) Edward \(\to\) Frances \(\to\) Brian \(\to\) Alan \(\to\) Jordan \(\to\) Victoria \(\to\) Maria \(\to\) Thomas \(\to\) Abigail \(\to\) Christopher \(\to\) Wayne \(\to\) Jacqueline \(\to\) Mark \(\to\) Justin \(\to\) Jack.

Because both Ruth and Gerald have directed paths that terminate at the same individual (Jack), Jack is a common descendant. No path exists from Ruth to Gerald or from Gerald to Ruth, so neither is an ancestor of the other. No common ancestor of Ruth and Gerald appears in any chain.

Thus only statement 1 is entailed by the given relations.
